metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [12. November 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.62

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [12. November 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.62
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.62
- Datum: 12.11.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
12. Nov. 1940
Dear Hannah, I did send you today a cable asking
for you to inform Friedental that I was informed today
that the Argentine ~~Consulate~~ {in London} has been instructed to
deliver a visa for him. I was here in private audience at the minister
of the Exterior Roca to ask him for three visas, one for Friedental
and he was so kind to grant it to me and as his secretary told me the
cables have gone already to London. Please help him with money for
the passage and as much as he wants; here in Buenos Aires I have
instructed my friends to be useful to him and also in Brazil he can
have opportunities. For the United States I could not help him for the
moment.
I have just returned from the tour in the province
which was as strenuous as successful - I am glad Lotte remained
in Buenos Aires, she would not have stood this strain, lectures, nights
in the train, and drives from 7 in the morning, receptions, photographs.
It was a sort of sensation, an author of Europe who speaks Spanish
and now it goes to Montevideo where I have to speak in a hall be-
fore 4000 - 5000 people, leaving behind our flowergarden - even
the W.C and the bidet are full of flowers for Lotte. But how happy
we shall be to have again a quiet life and not to rivalise with
cinema-stars. We have refused, Chile, Paraguay, Colombia, Cuba, we
have enough for the moment - enough of success, fees, flowers,
people and refugees. How we are longing to sit quietly again in
Bath!
A sad news was that our best friend in Rio, Hernandez Catá
pages.notes: Brief auf Hotelpapier (City Hotel, Buenos Aires). Handschrift in violetter Tinte. Die Seite endet mitten im Satz.

pages.transcription:
The ambassador of Cuba has been killed in an stupid
aeroplan-accident. Three days after his death a letter
of him ~~reaches~~ {would} me here, saying, that he wait with his
carf on the aerodrom, when we arrive - and he lost his
life meanwhile in a plane excursion. He was the kindest man
I have met since years and he guaranties for Friedental in
Cuba - I hope they did send the visa to Friedental from Ha-
vanna. You understand that the only way to be grateful for
the preference and happiness which we enjoy is that we try to
use here our influence to help to others. It is frightfully
difficult for there exits a secret order not to give any more
visas to Jews and only the minister of the Exterior could
personally break this iron rule. What times, - and how
often, you can not imagine to go our thoughts to you and
what we have too much of happiness here would be due
to you all. Now I have to work for two month on my book
on Brazil and then we will think over if we go to Newyork
- my sister in law is in contact with Eva and we get always
notices through her - not from Eva herself, who seems to be
too happy to write. Yours

Stefan Zweig
My dears, I am terribly busy, tired and still upset
about the news of the death of Catá, and that is the
only thing which spoils the pleasure of returning to
Rio to a normal working life and a beautiful landscape.
I shall write you at length immediately we arrive in Rio.
In the meantime kindest regards and kisses
Lotte
pages.notes: Zweite Seite des Briefes. Handschrift in violetter Tinte. Enthält eine Nachricht von Stefan Zweig und einen Nachsatz von Lotte Zweig.

pages.notes: Identisch mit Seite 3, jedoch mit aufgelegter Farbskala/Grauskala für Archivierungszwecke.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der kursiven Handschrift von Stefan Zweig. Die Korrekturen und Einfügungen sind eindeutig.
